jessica-ancona.text: Voted with a 7-0 council on Jan. 28, 2026 to accept a federal COPS hiring grant and raise Police Department staffing from 132 to 137 sworn officers ($1.03M total cost).

source.title: El Monte City Council Minutes, Jan. 28, 2026

jessica-ancona.text: Voted for Urgency Ordinance No. 3062 restricting use of city-owned or city-controlled property (7-0, Mar. 18, 2026); Ancona moved to open the public hearing; a public commenter addressed it as the urgency ordinance regarding immigration enforcement.

source.title: El Monte City Council Adjourned Meeting Minutes, Mar. 18, 2026

jessica-ancona.text: Platform: "Safe Neighborhoods" — strong police and fire services, homelessness outreach, illegal dumping/graffiti and code enforcement.
Platform: "City Hall has a responsibility to manage taxpayer dollars carefully"; pledges responsible budgeting, protecting reserves and opposing wasteful spending.
Platform commits to good-paying jobs and union job support, plus small-business assistance and workforce development.
Platform includes support for immigrant families under "Standing Up for El Monte Families."
Endorsed by the LA/Orange Counties Building and Construction Trades Council, SEIU Local 721, IBEW Local 11, Laborers Local 300, several Teamsters locals and SEIU 121RN.
Endorsed by the Los Angeles County Democratic Party.
City bio says she "supports smart conscious development and welcomes progress that considers community first."

source.title: City of El Monte - Mayor Jessica Ancona
